newsitem.title: UK: Orange Q2 subscriber base rises to 980,000.
newsitem.headline: Orange Q2 subscriber base rises to 980,000.

text.p: Britain's youngest mobile phone operator Orange Plc said on Tuesday that its subscriber base rose 86,000 in the second quarter of this year to 980,000.

Orange, which operates a purely digital network, also said that earnings before interest, tax and depreciation (EBITDA) had turned positive "in a significant milestone on the way to full profitability".
Since the start of the year its customer base has grown by 25 percent.
It said that churn had remained low in line with expectations with a rate of 19.9 percent over the past 12 months.

Analysts expect Orange, which has built on its reputation for innovation, to take the largest share of total net new customers although One-2-One, jointly owned by Cable & Wireless and US West Inc, is also expected to have reaped the benefit from new tariffs.
SBC Warburg expects One-2-One, which is not separately listed, to take 24 percent of net new connections.
Some analysts warn that tariffs in Britain's cellular market remain too high and will have to drop to European levels if industry consensus forecasts of subscriber growth are to be met.

Despite recent moves to cut prices, which have left tariffs at the bottom end of the market almost a third lower than in April, they remain more than 30 percent higher than in the high penetration high growth countries in Europe, according to Salomon Brothers.
